b27.text: The Allegro™ ACS723 current sensor IC is an economical and precise solution for AC or DC current sensing in industrial, commercial, and communication systems. The small package is ideal for space constrained applications while also saving costs due to reduced board area. Typical applications include motor control, load detection and management, switched-mode power supplies, and overcurrent fault protection.
b27.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b28.text: The device consists of a precise, low-offset, linear Hall sensor circuit with a copper conduction path located near the surface of the die. Applied current flowing through this copper conduction path generates a magnetic field which is sensed by the integrated Hall IC and converted into a proportional voltage. Device accuracy is optimized through the close proximity of the magnetic field to the Hall transducer. A precise, proportional voltage is provided by the low-offset, chopper-stabilized BiCMOS Hall IC, which includes Allegro’s patented digital temperature compensation, resulting in extremely accurate performance over temperature. The output of the device has a positive slope when an increasing current flows through the primary copper conduction path (from pins 1 through 4, to pins 5 through 8), which is the path used for current sensing. The internal resistance of this conductive path is 0.85 mΩ typical, providing low power loss.
b28.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b29.text: The terminals of the conductive path are electrically isolated from the sensor leads (pins 9 through 16). This allows the ACS723 current sensor IC to be used in high-side current sense applications without the use of high-side differential amplifiers or other costly isolation techniques.

b126.text: The change in sensor IC output in response to a 1A change through the primary conductor. The sensitivity is the product of the magnetic coupling factor $\left( \mathrm { G } / \mathrm { A } \right) \left( 1 \mathrm { G } = 0 . 1 \right.$ mT)and the linear IC amplifier gain (mV/G). The linear IC amplifier gain is programmed at the factory to optimize the sensitivity (mV/A) for the full-scale current of the device.
b126.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b127.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b128.text: The nonlinearity is a measure of how linear the output of the sensor IC is over the full current measurement range. The nonlinearity is calculated as:
b128.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b129.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b130.text: where $\mathrm { V _ { I O U T } ( I _ { P R ( m a x ) } ) }$ is the output of the sensor IC with the maximum measurement current flowing through it and $\mathrm { V _ { I O U T } } ( \mathrm { I _ { P R ( m a x ) } } / 2 )$ is the output of the sensor IC with half of the maximum measurement current flowing through it.
b130.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b131.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b132.text: The output of the sensor when the primary current is zero. For a unipolar supply voltage, it nominally remains at $0 . 5 \times \mathrm { V } _ { \mathrm { C C } }$ for a bidirectional device and $0 . 1 \times \mathrm { V } _ { \mathrm { C C } }$ for a unidirectional device. For example, in the case of a bidirectional output device, $\mathrm { v _ { C C } = }$ $5 . 0 \mathrm { V }$ translates into $\mathrm { V } _ { \mathrm { I O U T ( Q ) } } = 2 . 5 0 \mathrm { V }$ . Variation in $\mathrm { V _ { I O U T ( Q ) } }$ can be attributed to the resolution of the Allegro linear IC quiescent voltage trim and thermal drift.
b132.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b133.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b134.text: The deviation of the device output from its ideal quiescent value of $0 . 5 \times \mathrm { V } _ { \mathrm { C C } }$ (bidirectional) or $0 . 1 \times \mathrm { V } _ { \mathrm { C C } }$ (unidirectional) due to nonmagnetic causes. To convert this voltage to amperes, divide by the device sensitivity, Sens.
b134.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b135.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b136.text: The difference between the current measurement from the sensor IC and the actual current $\mathrm { ( I _ { P } ) }$ , relative to the actual current. This is equivalent to the difference between the ideal output voltage and the actual output voltage, divided by the ideal sensitivity, relative to the current flowing through the primary conduction path:
b136.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b137.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b138.text: The Total Output Error incorporates all sources of error and is a function of $\mathrm { I _ { P } }$ . At relatively high currents, $\mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { T O T } }$ will be mostly due to sensitivity error, and at relatively low currents, $\mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { T O T } }$ will be mostly due to Offset Voltage $( \mathrm { V _ { O E } } )$ . In fact, at $\mathrm { I _ { P } } = 0 , \mathrm { E _ { T O T } }$ approaches infinity due to the offset. This is illustrated in Figures 1 and 2. Figure 1 shows a distribution of output voltages versus $\mathrm { I _ { P } }$ at $2 5 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ and across temperature. Figure 2 shows the corresponding $\mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { T O T } }$ versus $\mathrm { I _ { P } }$

b149.text: The ACS723 works by sensing the magnetic field created by the current flowing through the package. However, the sensor cannot differentiate between fields created by the current flow and external magnetic fields. This means that external magnetic fields can cause errors in the output of the sensor. Magnetic fields which are perpendicular to the surface of the package affect the output of the sensor, as it only senses fields in that one plane. The error in Amperes can be quantified as:
b149.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b150.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b151.text: where B is the strength of the external field perpendicular to the surface of the package in Gauss, and $\mathrm { C _ { F } }$ is the coupling factor in G/A. Then, multiplying by the sensitivity of the part (Sens) gives the error in mV.
b151.source_file: /Users/192y/电气/抽样JSON（MInerU）/ACS723_数据手册/ACS723_数据手册_content_list.json

b152.text: For example, an external field of 1 Gauss will result in around 0.22 A of error. If the ACS723KMATR-10AB, which has a nominal sensitivity of 200 mV/A, is being used, that equates to 44 mV of error on the output of the sensor.

The ±3 sigma value for Total Error $( \mathrm { E _ { T O T } } )$ as a function of the sensed current $\mathrm { ( I _ { P } ) }$ is estimated as:
